# FDG8021

> DO use `Collection<T>` or a subclass of `Collection<T>` for properties or return values representing read/write collections.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3.2 Collection Properties and Return Values.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Not machine-checkable: whether a collection is meant to be read/write is design intent. CA1002 (FDG8014) reports List<T> in public signatures, the usual alternative to Collection<T>.

## From the book

```csharp
public Collection<Session> Sessions { get; }
```

If `Collection<T>` does not meet some requirement (e.g., the collection must not implement `IList`), use a custom collection by implementing `IEnumerable<T>`, `ICollection<T>`, or `IList<T>`.
